title: Monitoring, Ventilator Graphics & Patient Transport Quiz

questions.text: A ventilated patient's PIP increases from 28 to 46 cmH₂O over one hour. A ventilator check reveals Pplat is 27 cmH₂O. What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: Increased airway resistance — the large delta (PIP − Pplat = 19 cmH₂O) indicates an obstruction
Decreased lung compliance — both PIP and Pplat would be elevated
Auto-PEEP — the baseline pressure would also be elevated
Circuit disconnection — a low-pressure alarm would trigger
By programming an inspiratory hold, which halts gas flow and allows pressure to equilibrate
By measuring the peak pressure during a volume-control breath
By calculating PIP minus PEEP
By measuring pressure at the Y-piece during spontaneous breathing

questions.text: A patient's static compliance is calculated at 28 mL/cmH₂O. What does this indicate?

answers.text: Significantly decreased compliance — normal is 60–100 mL/cmH₂O; this suggests ARDS, atelectasis, or pulmonary fibrosis
Normal compliance — no adjustment is needed
Increased airway resistance requiring bronchodilator therapy
Auto-PEEP — the expiratory time must be lengthened

questions.text: On the flow-time scalar, the expiratory flow waveform does not return to the zero baseline before the next breath begins. What does this indicate?

answers.text: Auto-PEEP — gas is still flowing out when the next breath is triggered, indicating trapped gas
A circuit leak — volume is escaping the system
Flow starvation — the inspiratory flow is set too low
Normal pattern in pressure-control ventilation

questions.text: A ventilated patient on volume-control A/C shows a distinct downward dip in the pressure-time scalar during the inspiratory phase. What is the most appropriate intervention?

answers.text: Increase the peak inspiratory flow rate — the patient's demand is exceeding the delivered flow (flow starvation)
Increase the tidal volume — the patient needs more volume per breath
Switch to pressure control — it will automatically match the patient's flow demand
Increase PEEP — the patient is not being adequately recruited

questions.text: Which ventilator graphic best detects a circuit leak?

answers.text: Volume-time scalar — the tracing does not return to baseline at end-exhalation
Pressure-time scalar — baseline pressure rises above PEEP
Flow-time scalar — expiratory flow does not return to zero
P/V loop — the loop becomes wider than normal

questions.text: How often should a patient-ventilator system check be performed?

answers.text: At least every 2 hours on a scheduled basis, and also before ABGs, after setting changes, and after acute deterioration
Every 4 hours unless a specific change warrants earlier evaluation
Only when the physician orders it or the patient deteriorates
Every 30 minutes for the first 24 hours, then every 8 hours

questions.text: What is the maximum transport distance for which a rotary-wing (helicopter) aircraft is typically used?

answers.text: 80 to 150 miles
0 to 80 miles
150 to 300 miles
More than 150 miles

questions.text: During a CCATT flight at altitude, the ETT cuff pressure should be:

answers.text: Checked and adjusted before and after takeoff and landing — the cuff expands at altitude and may deflate during descent
Set to maximum pressure before takeoff to prevent aspiration
Deflated completely during flight to prevent tracheal injury
Left unchanged — cuff pressure is not affected by altitude

questions.text: What is the CCATT, and who are its three core members?

answers.text: Critical Care Air Transport Team — Critical Care Physician, Critical Care Nurse, and Respiratory Therapist
Comprehensive Combat Aeromedical Transport Team — Trauma Surgeon, Flight Medic, and Pararescueman
Critical Care Ambulatory Transport Team — Intensivist, RN, and EMT-Paramedic
Combat Critical Aeromedical Team — Critical Care Physician, Respiratory Therapist, and Pharmacist
